title: Command parity: onboard, graph/impact CLI, external MCP + backend-status readout
description: Ensure every graph-consuming surface works through the resolved backend and expose which engine is active. Verify `agent-bober onboard` produces all 5 artifacts on the code-review-graph backend (version line sourced from backendVersion, not tokensave), that `agent-bober impact` and `agent-bober graph` and src/mcp/server.ts construct and use the resolved backend, and add a backend-status readout (e.g. `agent-bober graph status`) printing the active engine id + version. All verified with fixtures/mocked transport per the fixtures-now decision.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors.

onboard: with the code-review-graph backend + mocked transport returning cr-graph search fixtures, `agent-bober onboard` writes all 5 markdown artifacts (README, architecture-overview, hotspots, knowledge-gaps, communities) to .bober/onboarding/, and the status/version line shows the cr-graph backendVersion (onboard.ts:134 no longer assumes manifest.tokensaveVersion for a non-tokensave backend). Unit/integration-tested.

impact + graph CLIs: src/cli/commands/impact.ts and src/cli/commands/graph.ts resolve and use the active backend; a test forcing graph.backend='code-review-graph' shows they operate through the cr-graph backend (mocked transport) and produce their reports.

External MCP server: src/mcp/server.ts exposes its graph tools backed by the resolved backend (not a hardcoded tokensave client). Verified by a test that constructs the server with graph.backend='code-review-graph'.

A backend-status readout exists (e.g. `agent-bober graph status`) that prints the active engine id and version (backendVersion), and indicates whether it was chosen by explicit config or auto-detection. Tested for both backends.

Selecting each backend in turn (graph.backend='tokensave' then 'code-review-graph') produces a working graph layer for that engine across onboard/impact/graph in tests. tokensave remains byte-identical. Full suite green (no NEW failures); lint clean.

nonGoals: Do NOT rework onboard.ts's data-gathering strategy (it keeps its 5 search() calls); only its backend source + version line change.
Do NOT add a live cr-graph run to default CI (fixtures/mocked transport for these tests).
Do NOT change the adapters from Sprints 5-6 or the tokensave path.
Do NOT add new graph capabilities beyond the backend-status readout.
stopConditions: onboard/impact/graph/mcp-server all work through the resolved backend for both engines; a backend-status readout shows the active engine; tokensave byte-identical; suite + lint green
definitionOfDone: Every graph-consuming surface (onboard, impact, graph, external MCP) operates through the resolved backend; onboard's version line uses backendVersion; a `graph status`-style readout prints the active engine id + version + selection source; both backends are exercised end-to-end via fixtures; tokensave byte-identical; suite + lint green.
assumptions: onboard.ts already gathers all data via graphClient.search() (119-126) and maps SearchHit -> OnboardingInputs (137-185), so it is backend-agnostic EXCEPT status.tokensaveVersion (134). Change that to manifest.backendVersion ?? prereq.version, and (optional) the DISABLED_MSG/arch-doc references can mention either engine.

impact.ts, graph.ts, mcp/server.ts were switched to resolveGraphBackend in Sprint 3; this sprint confirms they actually EXERCISE the resolved backend end-to-end (not just construct it) and adds coverage forcing the cr-graph backend.

The backend-status readout can extend the existing `graph` command group (src/cli/commands/graph.ts) with a `status` subcommand, or augment an existing status output, printing {engine id, version, selectedBy: 'config'|'auto-detect'}.
Tests mock the transport (feed cr-graph fixtures) so no live binary is needed; a skipIf live onboard against cr-graph is optional and, if added, must skip when the binary is absent.
onboard writes to .bober/onboarding/; tests can run it against a temp project root or assert on the composed artifacts in-memory to avoid polluting the repo.
generatorNotes:
Read FIRST: src/cli/commands/onboard.ts (full — esp. 119-185 gather+map and 134 version), src/cli/commands/impact.ts, src/cli/commands/graph.ts, src/mcp/server.ts (graph tool wiring), the Sprint-3 resolveGraphBackend, and the Sprint-5/6 cr-graph adapters + fixtures.

onboard: change status.tokensaveVersion source to backendVersion (manifest.backendVersion ?? prereq.version). Confirm onboard already flows through resolveGraphBackend (Sprint 3); if it still builds a bare tokensave backend, switch it. Add a test that runs onboard with the cr-graph backend + a mocked transport returning the semantic_search_nodes_tool fixture for the 5 search calls, asserting all 5 artifacts are written and the version line shows the cr-graph version.

impact/graph/mcp-server: add tests forcing graph.backend='code-review-graph' and assert the resolved backend is used end-to-end (mock transport). Fix any site that still assumes tokensave.

backend-status: add a `graph status` subcommand (or extend status output) printing engine id + version + selectedBy. Test for both backends.

Run `npm run build && npm run typecheck && npx vitest run` (full) + lint. Confirm tokensave onboard/impact/graph byte-identical. Commit `bober(sprint-7): command parity (onboard/impact/graph/mcp) through resolved backend + graph status readout`.
evaluatorNotes: sc-7-2: confirm onboard's version line no longer hardcodes/assumes tokensaveVersion for a cr-graph backend, and all 5 files are produced from cr-graph fixtures. sc-7-3/7-4: verify the tests actually FORCE graph.backend='code-review-graph' and that impact/graph/mcp-server use the cr-graph backend (not silently tokensave). sc-7-5: run the status readout for both backends and confirm it names the right engine + version + selection source. sc-7-6: flip the backend and confirm each engine yields a working graph layer; tokensave path byte-identical (existing onboard/impact/graph tests unchanged). Full suite: no new failures. Reject if any surface still hardcodes tokensave, or if onboard shows a tokensave version while running cr-graph.
